_comment: Prompts for the A2 CALIBRATION tasks k1-k4 (freeze-calib-a2.md).
`consult`, `tails` and `capture_instruction` are copied BYTE-FOR-BYTE from prompts-a1.json.
The calibration moves the turn ceiling and nothing else; a prompt that drifted between A1
and this measurement would confound the ceiling with the instruction.
Each body describes only what the checkout DOES, observed from the failing acceptance
checks, and never how to fix it. Every task declares set=development: these are development
tasks and run_arms_isolated accepts them; none is held-out evidence.
`environment` (added 2026-09-14, calibration config v2) states how to run the checkout. It is
appended IDENTICALLY to all three arms and names no task and no fix. It exists because A1 and
the v1 calibration rows measured agents spending turns rediscovering that the checkout is a
src/ layout -- with the network denied, the venv and pip attempts they reached for could not
have worked. That is harness friction, uniform across arms, and it confounds a turn-ceiling
measurement. Runs made before this block existed are config v1 and are NOT pooled with v2.
`environment` was REWRITTEN 2026-09-19 for configuration v3, and that is the only change:
no task body, tail, consult text or capture instruction is touched, so the requirement to
fix in `src/` AND extend the existing test suite stands exactly as registered.
Why: the v2 block documented `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest`, which passed the
environment gate and failed for the agent. The gate ran it under `zsh -c`; the arms' own
recorded `which -a python3` shows /usr/bin before /opt/homebrew, which is what a LOGIN zsh
produces -- /etc/zprofile runs path_helper, and the operator's ~/.zprofile that would put
Homebrew back in front is not readable inside the arm boundary. `python3` was therefore
3.9.6 without pytest for the agent and 3.14.7 with pytest for the gate. `No module named
pytest` appears in 10 of 11 failing v2 arm-runs and in all 16 passing ones.
PATH cannot carry the fix -- path_helper PREPENDS, so an inherited entry is pushed below
/usr/bin. `$A2_PYTHON` is set by the harness in `a1_config.child_env`, so the gate and the
runner read one value rather than each resolving their own, and the gate now runs every
documented command under BOTH shell startups and requires them to agree.
consult: Before your first source edit, consult any available prior-work memory: Nexus memory tools or `NOTES-FROM-EARLIER-WORK.md`. If neither is available, proceed using the repository. Treat prior notes as potentially outdated and verify relevant claims against current code.

tails.default: Fix the behaviour in `src/`, and extend the existing test suite to cover it. Do not change behaviour unrelated to this bug. When you are done, reply DONE.
tails.d4: Do not change behaviour unrelated to this. When you are done, reply DONE.

capture_instruction:
You are the first session to work in this repository, and a later session will work in it after you. Record what that later session would want to know, using the memory tools you have (`record`, and `revise` to correct something you already recorded).

**Before your first source edit, record at least one thing you have learned about this codebase.** Then keep recording as you go, rather than all at the end. Recording is not an afterthought to this task: a session that fixes the behaviour and records nothing has not done what it was asked.

Record four kinds of thing, and apply the test beside each one before recording it:
- `decision` — a choice already made in this codebase, and its reason. Could a reader reach this by reading the code as it stands?
- `constraint` — an invariant or convention the code holds to. Is it stated or evident in the code, the docs or the tests as they stand?
- `procedure` — how something is done in this repository. Did you actually do it this way?
- `failure` — something that went wrong and what it turned out to be. Did you observe it, rather than anticipate it?
Use `observation` only for something that fits none of those four.

Do not record:
1. Anything you can state only because you did this task — the change you made, where you made it, or a description of the defect specific enough to substitute for finding it.
2. Anything about the tests that judge this work: no test name, no assertion, no expected output.
3. Anything that is true only after your change. A convention your own fix introduces is not prior knowledge, however true it is once you are done.
4. The task statement, or anything that reads as an instruction for a later task.

The test that separates a recordable constraint from a leak is whether it names the convention or the violation. "Values of this kind are normalised before they are compared" is a convention, discoverable in the code as it stands, and is recordable. "This particular path forgets to normalise them" is the defect you were asked to find, and is not.

k1.body:
In this Click checkout, callbacks registered with `ctx.call_on_close()` are not all run when an eager option ends the invocation with `ctx.exit()`.

Reproduction: declare two eager options whose callbacks each call `ctx.call_on_close(...)` to register a cleanup, and where the second option's callback also calls `ctx.exit()`. Invoking the command with both options, in the order `--option-with-callback --force-exit`, should run both registered cleanups; only one runs. Invoking them in the order `--force-exit --option-with-callback` should run only the exiting option's cleanup, which is the behaviour the eagerness ordering implies.

The same defect leaks real state. An option whose callback raises a global logger's level and registers a `call_on_close` to reset it leaves the logger raised after the command exits, because the reset never runs.

k2.body:
In this Click checkout, an option declared `is_flag=True` together with an explicit `type=` produces the wrong value when the flag is passed on the command line.

Reproduction: `@click.option("--foo", is_flag=True, type=bool)` echoes `False` when invoked with `--foo`, where `True` is expected. With `type=bool, default=True`, invoking with `--foo` echoes `True` where `False` is expected. `type=click.BOOL` behaves the same way as `type=bool` in both cases, and `type=str` with `--foo` passed echoes an empty line where `True` is expected.

Omitting the flag behaves correctly in every one of those cases; only passing it is wrong.

k3.body:
In this Click checkout, when several flag options share one parameter name and more than one supplies a default, the wrong default is chosen.

Reproduction: a command with `@click.option("--red", "color", flag_value="red")` and `@click.option("--green", "color", flag_value="green", default=True)` should echo `green` when invoked with no arguments. A command with those two options declared in the other order, `--red` carrying `default=True` and `--green` carrying none, should echo `red` when invoked with no arguments.

Passing a flag explicitly selects that flag's value correctly in both commands; only the no-argument case is wrong.

k4.body:
In this Click checkout, the eagerness of the help option generated from `help_option_names` is not respected, because the option is generated more than once.

Reproduction: a command declared `context_settings={"help_option_names": ("--my-help",)}` with two options whose callbacks echo and then call `ctx.exit()` — `-a` declared without `is_eager`, and `-b` declared `is_eager=True`. Invoking with `--my-help` should print the help text and exit without running either callback. Invoking with `-a` should run only `-a`'s callback. Invoking with `-a -b` should run only `-b`'s callback, because `-b` is eager and `-a` is not.

environment: How to run this checkout: it is a `src/` layout and is NOT installed. A prepared interpreter is provided as `$A2_PYTHON`, with the test runner already available; use it rather than plain `python3`, which on this machine resolves to a different interpreter that has no `pytest`. Import the checkout with `PYTHONPATH=src "$A2_PYTHON" ...`, and run tests with `PYTHONPATH=src "$A2_PYTHON" -m pytest <paths> -q`. There is no network: `pip`, `uv` and any download will fail, and nothing needs to be installed. Write any scratch or reproduction file inside the checkout rather than in /tmp.
